text:
Sam H: FYI — customer GW-ACME in eu-west-1 reports inference pod crashes on Private cluster after our recent kernel+driver push.
Maria V: Ugh. Do we have logs from their node or the container?
Sam H: Got a stack from the support bundle. Short version: libnvidia complains, container fails during nccl init. Example: 
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_diagnostics.cc:xxx] namespaceError: couldn't find libnvidia-ml.so
2026-03-18 10:12:01 ERROR runtime: failed to initialize ncclCommRank: NCCL version mismatch (required 2.14 vs loaded 2.12)
```
Sam H: They say they didn't change anything on their side — running our onprem package pinned to 525.89 driver and kernel 5.15. But we rolled a kernel+driver package last week for new GPUs.
Jon P: Do we have compatibility matrix docs? I thought 525.x was EOL for some kernels.
Maria V: Our internal matrix (private deployments) lists: driver 525.* supported with kernel 5.15-5.19 but only when NCCL 2.14 backcompat applied by our runtime shim. Customer's bundle shows NCCL 2.12 in /opt/nccl.
Sam H: Support says customer has an older NCCL installed at /opt/nccl and their package path precedes our runtime libs. Their system is effectively using distro NCCL not Redwood-provided one.
ops-oncall: @Sam H can you paste the environment and LD_LIBRARY_PATH from the failing container?
Sam H: From the crash container: 
```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/nccl/lib:/usr/local/nvidia/lib:/usr/local/nvidia/lib64
NCCL_VERSION=2.12.10
nvidia-smi:
Tue Mar 16 09:59:12 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 11.8     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Jon P: The driver version there is 525.85 but our runtime now expects a minimum NCCL 2.14 because of multi-node allreduce optimizations. If the customer forces /opt/nccl first, mismatch is expected.
Maria V: Customer insists matrix says they should be fine — they showed our public-support-matrix PDF which lists 525.x as supported. They claim we shifted a requirement without notice.
ops-oncall: Can we check the exact commit that bumped NCCL requirement?
Sam H: It was the runtime change in repo: inference-runtime@v1.8.3 that toggled NCCL collective protocol (PR 8421) — merged 2026-03-10. Release notes mentioned performance fixes but not the hard dependency.
Maria V: We're stuck between two problems: (1) our release increased minimum NCCL compat, (2) private deployments can have vendor-local NCCL installed which we don't override.
Jon P: Short-term mitigation: we can modify the onprem package to set /usr/local/redwood/lib before /opt in LD_LIBRARY_PATH and ship a tiny wrapper script. That would avoid the customer needing to touch system libs.
Sam H: Customer is sensitive about us changing their nodes. They want us to prove the matrix mismatch first.
ops-oncall: Suggested steps for triage: 
1) capture `ldd` of failing binary inside container
2) run `strings /usr/local/redwood/lib/libnccl.so | grep 2.` to show versions
3) test an alternate startup with our library path prepended (non-destructive)
4) if that fixes, offer a hotfix tarball and an upgrade plan
Jon P: I'll run a quick repro in a lab node with kernels 5.15 and 5.19 and both NCCL 2.12/2.14 to validate.
Sam H: Customer sent this patch of their sysinfo: 
```
Kernel: 5.15.0-70-generic
Packages: cuda-11-8 (installed), nccl-2.12.x (manual install), nvidia-driver-525.85
```
Maria V: Note — some vendor OVAs pin /opt/nccl via modulefiles. That explains why container uses it by default.
ops-oncall: Who owns the communications with the customer on a patch? Support wants a single approved artifact to send.
Sam H: I'll own the hotfix tarball if eng signs off. Planning: build a wrapper `redwood-ld-prepend.sh` that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH and execs our runtime. Non-invasive.
Jon P: If we ship that, ops should also include a validation script that checks `nvidia-smi` vs `ldconfig -p` and prints NCCL/driver mismatch warnings.
Maria V: Also need a comms note acknowledging we changed runtime requirements in v1.8.3 and apologizing for not surfacing it in the public matrix. Ops/legal might want the wording reviewed.
ops-oncall: Action items recap: 
- Jon: repro matrix tests and confirm which combos fail (ETA 4h)
- Sam: prepare hotfix wrapper tarball + validation script (ETA 6h)
- Maria: draft customer comms and internal blameless postmortem note (ETA EOD)
- ops-oncall: coordinate support ticket and staging rollout plan

deploy-bot: deploy-notice: rolling canary for inference-runtime v1.8.3 to private-edge group completed at 2026-03-10T22:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

Sam H: One more note — long-term we should update our onprem installer to either vendor-lock our redistributable NCCL or run a preflight that detects & fails early with an actionable message.
Maria V: Agreed. I'll add a story to the product board for matrix clarity + preflight checks.
Jon P: Found repro: kernel 5.15 + driver 525 + system NCCL 2.12 => fails init. kernel 5.19 + driver 525 + our NCCL 2.14 => passes. I'll paste logs in a follow-up.
Sam H: Thanks — let's sync after Jon's repro.
ops-oncall: tagging #support to prep ticket bundle and a one-off patch channel. :thumbsup:
Maria V: pinging @legal to review comms before we send to GW-ACME (they're enterprise).
Sam H: closing loop for now. Will push hotfix tarball to S3 for support to pull once Jon confirms.
